title: Massive News for AI Stock Investors
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garbled in places
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA weighs the good and bad news for AI investors in a macro video with no new explicit call. The good news is US non-farm productivity, up 3.6% annualised (after 2.1% in the second quarter), with unit labour costs down 0.7% — the first decline since the second quarter of 2025. He reads this as the foundational AI demand case: enterprises spend tens of trillions of dollars a year on labour that AI can make more productive, and falling unit labour costs are disinflationary, easing pressure on the Fed; he cautions that productivity is a volatile, hard-to-measure statistic. The bad news is the US midterm results, which empowered local opponents of data-centre builds and add friction — delays and concessions such as community funds — on top of existing constraints: power, memory supply, circular financing, and hyperscalers borrowing and selling stock to fund capex. Slower buildouts stretch out component sales for Nvidia, AMD, Intel, Micron and SK Hynix rather than cancelling them, and he has long called for a slower, more prudent buildout pace. He is not selling and would add selectively to names already rated cheap — Nvidia, Micron, Qualcomm and Broadcom — but will not go all-in. Nvidia reports on 17 November, which he will cover live for members. No call-event is recorded; NVDA, MU, QCOM and AVGO remain rated BUY.
